question.erotisi: The Society of Friends was founded:
question.sxolio: Its founders, Nikolaos Skoufas, Athanasios Tzakalov and Emmanuel Xanthos, succeeded with extreme secrecy to mobilze all the forces of the nation for the preparation of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: The Society of Friends placed the leadership of the Revolution in the hands of Alexandros Ypsilantis, because:
question.sosti: he was a worthy military officer of high rank in the Russian army
question.latos1: he belonged to the circle of the Secret Authority
question.latos2: he held a leading role in the Orlov revolt
question.sxolio: The Society of Friends at the beginning had no leader. When Kapodistrias declined the position, the Friends turned to Alexandros Ypsilantis, born in a Phanariot family and military officer in the Russian army, who in 1820 undertook the leadership.

question.erotisi: Alexandros Ypsilantis fought a crucial battle in Moldavia-Wallachia in 1821 and specifically:
question.sxolio: At the meeting of the Society of Friends at Izmail, the declaration of the Revolution was decided as well as the descent of Ypsilantis to the Peloponnese. Ypsilantis, however, decided that the Revolution should start at Jassy, where he proceeded to mark its beginning with the proclamation «Fight for faith and country».

question.erotisi: Adamantios Korais supported the Greek Revolution with
question.latos1: the writing of the Constitution of Troezen
question.latos2: donations for the foundation of schools in Ioannina
question.sxolio: Adamantios Korais published patriotic pamphlets and works of ancient Greek writers with forewords, in order to present his views on education and language.

question.erotisi: The assembly at Vostitsa (modern Aigio) took place in January 1821 with the aim to:
question.sosti: take decisions about the beginning of the Revolution
question.latos1: declare the Revolution in the Peloponnese
question.latos2: organize fundraisers for supporting the Struggle
question.sxolio: The assembly at Vostitsa was the first secret assembly of the Friends in the Peloponnese before the start of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: Who of the following played an important role in the assembly of Vostitsa?
question.sxolio: Alexandros Ypsilantis, leader of the Society of Friends since 1820, appointed Papaflessas as his representative and responsible for going to Moreas and the islands, carrying instructions about the beginning of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: Who of the following did not participate in the assembly of Vostitsa?
question.sxolio: Theodoros Kolokotronis reached the Peloponnese in January 1821. He took refuge in Mani, in the house of the notable Mourtzinos for protection, because the Turks had declared him an outlaw, and began to have contacts with the notables and captains of the Peloponnese for the preparation of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: The first city of the Peloponnese that was liberated from the Turks was:
question.sxolio: After the meeting in Vostitsa, the notables of the city began to recruit new members, a fact that did not go unnoticed by the Turks and for this reason they negotiated with the notables their safe departure from the city. When the Turks left, Andreas Londos raised the revolutionary flag, red with black cross.

question.erotisi: On 25 March, Paleon Patron Germanos and Andreas Londos raised the revolutionary flag in Patras. The Turks took refuge in the fort of the city and:
question.sosti: the siege was broken soon by the Ottoman troops, women and children were slaughtered and captured
question.latos1: the siege was lifted after the surrender of the besieged Turks due to the lack of food and ammunition
question.latos2: the siege was lifted after the reinforcement of the besiegers and ferocious battles
question.sxolio: Due to bad organization, lack of armament, attack of the Ottoman army, collaboration of the English consul with the Turks, but also due to disputes between notables and military men, the occupation of Patras failed.

question.erotisi: Athanasios Kanakaris took part in the siege of Patras. Later he served as:
question.sosti: vice-president in the First National Assembly
question.sxolio: Athanasios Kanakaris of Patras was a notable and in the First National Assembly was elected vice-president. Occasionally he replaced the president, Alexandros Mavrokordatos.

question.erotisi: After the declaration of the Revolution in Patras one of the first committees for the coordination of operations was established. How was it called?
question.sxolio: The Achaean Directorate, of which Paleon Patron Germanos was appointed honorary head, handed over a letter to the consuls of the foreign powers, specifying the aim of the Revolution and asking for their favour and protection.

question.erotisi: The liberation of Patras from the Turks took place:
question.sxolio: On 23 June 1822, Kolokotronis lifted the siege of Patras, because, despite the Grrek successes, the Executive did not offer him the food supplies, ammunition and men he had asked for. On 3 October 1828 the Third French Division, commanded by the French general Schneider, landed in Patras and the next day occupied the fort of the city.

question.erotisi: The occupation of Kalamata by Petrobey Mavromichalis and Theodoros Kolokotronis took place on:
question.sxolio: The Maniots reached the outskirts of Kalamata on 22 March and occupied the surrounding hills. Arnaoutoglou Aga realised that he could not flee to Tripolitsa and decided to resist. When though in the morning of the 23rd March the revolutionaries entered the city, he surrendered. After the liberation of Kalamata the Revolution broke also out in Mani.

question.erotisi: In which newspaper was the first proclamation of the Messinian Senate published?
question.sxolio: The «Salpinx Heleniki/ Trumpet Greek» was the first newspaper printed in Greece. It was printed in Kalamata on 1st August 1821 in a small printing press that Dimitrios Ypsilantis had brought from Trieste. It published a total of three issues, on the 1st, 5th and 20th of August. In the third issue the proclamation of the Messinian Senate was published.

question.erotisi: Who signed the first proclamation of the Messinian Senate?
question.sxolio: The political and diplomatic document was signed by Petrobey Mavromichalis, notable of Mani, member of the Society of Friends, leading military and political figure of the Revolution. It proclaimed the beginning of the Greek Revolution and asked for the contribution of the European states.

question.erotisi: The Messinian Senate, one of the first forms of central administration of the revolted Greeks, was set up at the beginning of the Revolution:
question.sxolio: The Messinian Senate was formed in Kalamata on 24 March 1821, after the liberation of the city. It issued a manifesto to the European powers, titled «Warning to the European courts», and coordinated the actions of the revolted Greeks in the Peloponnese.

question.erotisi: The statue of Patriarch Gregory V stands at the entrance:
question.latos2: of the National Historical Museum (Old Parliament Building)
question.sxolio: In 1871, during the celebration of the fifty-year anniversary of the Greek Revolution, the Patriarch's bones were relocated from Odessa to Athens and were deposited in a marble larnax in the Mitropolis of Athens. In 1872 his statue was erected, funded by Georgios Averof, and placed at the entrance of the University of Athens.

question.erotisi: Gregory V served three times as Patriarch of Constantinople and is honoured as a national martyr because:
question.sosti: he found a torturous death by the Turks
question.latos1: he took care of the refugees from the destruction of Chios
question.latos2: he fought and fell heroically in the battle of Maniaki
question.sxolio: On 10 April 1821, after the service of Easter, the Patriarch was arrested by the Turks, deposed and put in prison. In the afternoon of the same day he was hanged in the central gate of the Patriarchate, where he remained hanged for three days, being disgraced by the mob.

question.erotisi: The following stanza refers to the death of Patriarch Gregory V. To which poem does it belong?@Mourn you all. Dead is@the leader of the Church@mourn you, mourn, hanged@as if he were some murderer.
question.latos2: «The rock and the wave», Aristotle Valaoritis
question.sxolio: Special reference to the hanging of Patriarch Gregory V is made by our national poet, Dionysios Solomos, in his poem «Hymn to Liberty» (stanzas 132-138).

question.erotisi: As a tribute to the Patriarch:
question.sosti: the central gate of the Patriarchate in Constantinople remains closed
question.latos1: the central gate of the Patriarchate in Constantinople remains open
question.latos2: the Patriarchate in Constantinople has been named after him
question.sxolio: The central gate of the Patriarchate, where Gregory V was hanged, remains closed and sealed until today, as a tribute to him. To the Patriarchate one enters only from the lateral gates.

question.erotisi: The first important victory of the Revolution, decisive for its consolidation was:
question.latos1: the battle at the Chani (Inn) of Gravia
question.latos2: the surrender of the fort of Monemvasia
question.sxolio: After a six-month long siege, Tripolis was occupied on 23 September 1821. After the fall of the city, the Turkish resistance was put down in the Peloponnese, the siege of its forts continued and abundant spoils came in the hands of the Greeks.

question.erotisi: Who is the poet who wrote the verses?@Let those who heavy feel@the cupreous hand of fear@under slavery's yoke live@Mettle and virtue@is what Freedom wants.
question.sxolio: The verses belong to the poem of Andreas Kalvos «Ode fourth [IV], to Samos».

question.erotisi: To which battle of 1821 do the verses of the demotic song refer?@Diakos remained under fire with eighteen men.@For three hours he fought against eighteen thousand men.@His rifle exploded and broke into pieces.@He drew his sword and rushed into the battle,@killed countless Turks in sixty tabouria (bulwarks) and seven bouloukbasides (army officers).@But his sword broke at the handle,@and Diakos fell alive into the hands of the enemy who took him to the pasha,@a thousand soldiers in the front and a thousand in the rear.
question.sxolio: On 23 April 1821 Athanasios Diakos undertook to intercept the forces of Omer Vryonis at the bridge of Alamana. After the retreat of the corps of Dyovouniotis and Panourgias, who defended the surrounding areas, Diakos remained in the battle and wounded was captured. He found a torturous death in Lamia. His bravery was praised in the demotic song of Diakos.

question.erotisi: For the contribution of aid to the revolted Greeks, from 1821 onward Philhellenic Committees were set up in various countries. The first ones were set up:
question.sxolio: In setting up the committees a leading role was held by university professors who were writing articles in support of the Revolution, but also bankers, as the Swiss John-Gabriel Eynard, who later undertook the founding of the National Bank of Greece.

question.erotisi: The victory at the Chani (Inn) of Gravia in May 1821 is greatly due to the strategic genius of:
question.sxolio: Odysseas Androutsos proposed the fortification of the chani (inn), where from they could put up important resistance against the large army of Omer Vryonis. The victory was of great significance, because it obstructed the descent of the Ottoman army to the Peloponnese and therefore the Revolution was centered in Central Greece (Sterea Hellas).

question.erotisi: On 27 May 1821 Jacob Tombazis and Dimitrios Papanikolis set fire to the Turkish two-deck frigate in the naval battle of:
question.sxolio: The success of the Greeks was great, but it had a tragic consequence, the destruction of Kydonies in Asia Minor by the Ottomans, fifteen days later.

question.erotisi: At the end of July 1822 Dramalis attacked with a large army the revolted Greeks. Who were the chieftains who confronted him and where?
question.sosti: Kolokotronis and Nikitas Stamatelopoulos at Dervenakia
question.sxolio: Kolokotronis did not believe the rumors about the reoccupation of Tripolitsa and ordered the Greeks to intercept Dramalis' return to Corinth, fighting a battle in the narrow passes of Dervenakia. Dramalis' army dissolved and huge quantities of spoils fell in the hands of the Greeks.

question.erotisi: In the naval battle of Patras, on 20 February 1822, ships of the three islands, Hydra, Spetses and Psara, under the command of Miaoulis:
question.latos1: set fire to the flagship of the Ottoman fleet
question.sxolio: It was the first clash in which no fire-ships were used. After a ferocious naval battle, many damages were caused to the Ottoman fleet, which was forced to take refuge at Zakynthos.

question.erotisi: To the success of the siege of Nafplio, which surrendered in December 1822, it also contributed its naval blockade by the ships:
question.sxolio: Laskarina Bouboulina led the way in the siege of Nafplio. The naval blockade of the city prevented, in combination with the activity of the ships which moved in the Aegean and reinforced the siege of forts, the landing of army in the Peloponnese in the first year of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: The attempt of the Ottoman fleet to land on Mykonos in early October 1822 was fought off by the brave resistance of the inhabitants. Among them, as historians mention, a woman fought, too. Who was she?
question.sxolio: Manto Mavrogenous, born in a Phanariot family and one of the most impotant female figures of the Revolution, led the way in the uprising of Mykonos against the Turks. She equipped with armament ships and military corps with her own money and publisized the Struggle with her letters to the Philhellenes of Europe.

question.erotisi: On 20 December 1821 the works of the First National Assembly began in the village of Piada, near ancient Epidaurus. In the First National Assembly:
question.sosti: the Provisional Regime of Greece was voted
question.latos1: Theodoros Kolokotronis was appointed commander-in-chief of the Peloponnese
question.latos2: the course of the diplomatic discussions with the European courts was defined
question.sxolio: The First National Assembly voted the «Provisional Regime of Greece», a work of a multi-member committee, which was called «provisional», due to the need to appease the European Courts in relation to the negative for the revolutionary movements circumstances of the time.

question.erotisi: The two bodies of Administration that were established in the First National Assembly were:
question.sxolio: In the First National Assembly of Epidaurus it was defined that the Administration will consist of two bodies serving one-year term, the Executive with five members and the Legislative with seventy members.

question.erotisi: As president of the Executive body the First National Assembly elected:
question.sxolio: His alliance with the notables gave to the Phanariot Alexandros Mavrokordatos the opportunity to be elected president of the first National Assembly of Epidaurus and president of the Executive Body.

question.erotisi: The Provisional Regime of Epidaurus, which defined the political principles of the revolted areas, determined:
question.sosti: the «merit» of each one as unique criterion for the election to public offices
question.latos1: the founding of a network of monitorial schools
question.latos2: the division of the revolted territory into provinces
question.sxolio: The Provisional Regime protected individual rights, equality before the law and introduced the representative system of election, abolishing at the same time local or class privileges.

question.erotisi: Which important naval victory of the Greeks took place on 7 June 1822?
question.sosti: the burning of the Ottoman fleet at Chios
question.latos1: the blockade of the Ottoman fleet at Sfakteria
question.latos2: the crushing defeat of the Ottoman fleet at Gerontas
question.sxolio: After the Massacre of Chios, about sixty Greek ships were gathered at Psara and sailed away to Chios, expecting favourable weather conditions for launching an attack with fire-ships. The night of 6th to 7th June 1822 the flagship of the Ottoman fleet was blown up by a fire-ship.

question.erotisi: Two famous mariners attempted to set fire to the Ottoman fleet on 7 June 1822 near Chios. Who were they?
question.sxolio: Kanaris attached the fire-ship to the Turkish flagship, which was blown up. The fire-ship of Pipinos approached the sub-flagship, he did not though manage to blow it up, causing however several damages. The victims were far too many, among them the admiral Kara Ali.

question.erotisi: Who was the great painter who depicted the setting of fire to the Ottoman flagship at Chios?
question.sxolio: Nikiphoros Lytras painted the similarly called painting around 1866-1870. Konstantinos Kanaris is shown standing on a boat with his companions, the fire-ship men, as they sail away from the Ottoman fragship, having already managed to burn it. The Greek flag appears rising from the boat.

question.erotisi: The Greek ships in the years 1821-1822
question.sosti: blocked the replenishment of the forts of the Peloponnese
question.latos1: averted the landing of Ibrahim in the Peloponnese
question.latos2: achieved important victories in naval battles south of the Peloponnese
question.sxolio: The Ottoman fleet did not manage to replenish the forts of the Peloponnese, because it was obstructed by the fire-ships. In 1822 Dramalis was deprived of valuable provisions, Nafplio was besieged and surrendered, the fire-ships prevented the occupation of Hydra and Spetses and the Ottoman fleet took refuge in Dardanelia.

question.erotisi: After which battle did the first siege of Missolonghi take place?
question.sxolio: After the crushing defeat of the Greek divisions in the Battle of Peta, on 4 July 1822, where many Philhellenes were also killed, the Turkish forces moved towards Western Greece, with the aim to suppress the revolution there, focusing on Missolonghi.

question.erotisi: Who was the politician who played a leading role in the organization of defence during the first siege of Missolonghi?
question.sxolio: Alexandros Mavrokordatos organized the defence of the city, beginning by repairing the wall and the bastions and cleaning the moat. In order for those defending the city to appear more that they actually were, he attached many bayonets to wooden poles on the wall. Furthermore, he mobilized the Peloponnesians and the naval islands, which sent reiforcements for the defence of the city.

question.erotisi: When did the first siege of Missolonghi take place?
question.sxolio: The first siege of Missolonghi lasted from 25 October 1822 to 31 December 1822. The Ottoman forces lifted the siege after the brave resistance of the defenders of Missolonghi.

question.erotisi: Who was the leader of the Ottoman Turks during the first siege of Missolonghi?
question.sxolio: After the fall of Souli, the Turks under the leadership of Kioutachis and Omer Bryonis laid siege to Missolonghi. After the failed attempt to occupy the city, on Christmas night 1822, they lifted the siege and abandoned the camp, leaving behind cannons and ammunition.

question.erotisi: «If only one day, hero Markos, me too, should meet such a death.». Who was the fighter who said the above phrase?
question.sxolio: During the transportation of Markos Botsaris' body to Missolonghi, the brave men who carried him made a stop for a while in the narthex of Proussou Monastery, where Georgios Karaiskakis was lying ill. He kissed him saying «If only one day, hero Markos, me too, should meet such a death».

question.erotisi: The night of the 8th to the 9th of August 1823, Greek troops defeated the Ottomans at Kefalovryso of Karpenissi. Who was the chieftain in charge of the battle?
question.sxolio: Markos Botsaris, according to his own attack plan, launched an attack after the sunset against the enemy camp, targeting the tents of the commanders. A bullet that hit him in the eye proved fatal. His fellow fighters transported his body to Missolonghi, where he was buried with great honours on 10 August.

question.erotisi: In the summer of 1823 the Ottomans launched a campaign with the aim to:
question.latos1: suppress the relovution in the Peloponnese
question.latos2: suppress the uprising of Ali Pasha
question.sxolio: In 1823 the Turks, after the failure of the preceding campaigns, sent their main forces against Western Greece, but suffered losses and retreated to Arta.

question.erotisi: The setback of the Greek revolution began:
question.sxolio: In 1823 civil war broke out between the notables and the military men, a fact that was a setback for the military operations of the Greeks.

question.erotisi: In 1824 the Greek ships prevented the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet from attacking Samos by their victory:
question.sosti: in the naval battle in the bay of Gerontas
question.latos1: in the naval battle in the bay of Tsesme
question.latos2: in the naval battle of Navarino
question.sxolio: On 29 August 1824 the Greek ships won a victory in the naval battle of Gerontas. The Ottoman fleet retreated into Dardanelia and the Egyptian one to Souda of Crete.

question.erotisi: After the surrender of Neokastro, in 1825, there was a fear that the Egyptian fleet would attempt an attack on Hydra and Spetses. Greek ships succeeded in putting it off in the naval battle:
question.sxolio: According to Sachtouris, one of the commanders of the Greek ships, the naval battle of Kafireas, in the strait between Andros and Cavo d' Oro, ended with great losses for the enemy in ships, ammunition and men, forcing the enemy fleet to retreat. Decisive was also the action of the fire-ships of Matrozos and Boutis from Hydra.

question.erotisi: Which is the important naval island that was venerated by our national poet in the verses: @«[…] Glory walking alone@recalls the gallant young men@on her head she wears a wreath@made of what little grass@had remained on the desolate earth»
question.sxolio: Psara, a naval island with important fleet, was destroyed on 21 June 1824 by the Ottoman forces. Its destruction was venerated in 1825 by Dionysios Solomos in the epigram «the Destruction of Psara».

question.erotisi: Kolokotronis did not succeed in repelling the invasion of Ibrahim Pasha in the Peloponnese, because:
question.latos1: he was fighting in Roumeli (Central Greece)
question.sxolio: Kolokotronis and other chieftains were imprisoned because of the civil wars. Their release was demanded by the then Minister of Internal Affairs, Papaflessas, so as to be able to confront Ibrahim's attack, which was putting at risk the Revolution.

question.erotisi: An attempt to intercept the attack of Ibrahim was made by:
question.sxolio: On 20 May 1825 Grigorios Dikaios or Papaflessas attempted to intercept Ibrahim's advance to Maniaki of Messinia. The Greek forces were defeated, himself was killed, and subsequently Ibrahim occupied without resistance Kyparissia, Kalamata and many parts of Messinia, which he burnt down.

question.erotisi: The Greek forces intercepted the advance of Ibrahim in the Peloponnese:
question.sxolio: On 13 June 1825 Makrygiannis, Konstantinos Mavromichalis and Dimitrios Ypsilantis barricated themselves in the village of Myloi and confronted successfully the consecutive attacks of Ibrahim, who having failed to occupy Nafplio, burnt down Argos and returned to Tripolis.

question.erotisi: At the end of July 1827 Ibrahim organized a campaign in Mani. The Maniots:
question.latos2: abandoned their homes and took refuge on the mountains
question.sxolio: The Maniots confronted Ibrahim successfully. The latter repeated the attacks in Mani to no avail.

question.erotisi: The exodus of Missolonghi took place after a siege of many months in April of …:
question.sxolio: On 5 April 1826 G. Androutsos sent a letter to the notables of Spetses, to inform them that the inhabitants of Missolonghi decided «to exit storming out, rapier in hand, those who were going to die, die with glory and for the Country or surrender». The night of the 10th to the 11th of April 1826 the inhabitants of Missolonghi attempted the Exodus.

question.erotisi: Who was the acclaimed painter who depicted the personified Greece in the ruins of Missolonghi?
question.sxolio: The painting of the French artist Eugene Delacroix depicts the personified Greece in Greek traditional costume, standing on the ruins of Missolonghi, which have fallen over a fighter. A black man with yellow turban symbolizes the enemy.

question.erotisi: How was the city of Missolonghi named?
question.sxolio: On 22 April 1937, by the decision of Georgios II, Missolonghi was named «Sacred City of Missolonghi». Also, the Palm Sunday of each year, the anniversary of the heroic exodus, was established as a day of national celebration.

question.erotisi: Miaoulis' failure to approach Missolonghi determined the decision for Exodus. Under the command of which chieftains did the Exodus take place?
question.sosti: Notis Botsaris, Dimitrios Makris and Kitsos Tzavelas
question.latos1: Alexandros Mavrokordatos, Georgios Karaiskakis and Odysseas Androutsos
question.latos2: Ioannis Papadiamantopoulos, Dimitrios Themelis and Georgios Kanavos
question.sxolio: On the night of the 10th of April 1826, the inhabitants of Missolonghi arranged their forces in three divisions. In the middle of the triangle formed by these divisions, they placed the women and children. Georgios Karaiskakis, who had undertaken the mission to attack from the slopes of Zygos as a diversion, did not manage to put the plan in action, as Ibrahim received inforation about the movements of the besieged.

question.erotisi: The treaty of London was signed in 1827 by:
question.latos2: England and the Third National Assembly
question.sxolio: England, France and Russia signed the treaty, aiming at settling the Greek cause. On 6 August 1827 the Treaty was published in the «Independent Newspaper of Greece».

question.erotisi: The treaty of London of 1827 was particularly important for the course of the Revolution, because it provided for:
question.sosti: intervention of the Great Powers after the end of hostilities
question.latos1: loans and ammunition to the Greeks
question.latos2: creation of an independent Greek state
question.sxolio: According to the terms of the Treaty, the Great Powers were committed to undertake the task of pacification in the region, even if they were to face reactions from the Ottoman empire and the revolted Greeks.

question.erotisi: The first country of the Great Powers that supported the Greek Revolution was:
question.sxolio: In 1823 the minister of Foreign Affairs George Canning recognized the Greeks as a force in war. This strategic movement aimed, among other things, at impeding the influence of the homodox Russia on the Greeks.

question.erotisi: The first country of the Great Powers that supported financially the Greek Revolution was:
question.sxolio: The Greek Administration turned to England, to conclude two loans, for the needs of the Struggle. The financial houses of London disbursed in 1824 and 1825 the «loans of independence», of which only a small part reached Greece for the needs of the Struggle.

question.erotisi: On the flagship of Jacob Tombazis it was decided for the first time to use fire-ships in the struggle against the Ottoman fleet. How was his flagship called?
question.sxolio: The bow of the flagship is on display in the National and Historical Museum in Athens.

question.erotisi: The name «Akti/Coast Miaoulis» in Piraeus was given in honour of the fighter Andreas Miaoulis, because:
question.latos2: he defeated in a naval battle the Ottoman fleet at this spot
question.sxolio: The ship owner, politician and admiral Andreas Miaoulis was born on Hydra in 1769 and died in Piraeus in 1835. He was distinguished in the naval struggle of the Revolution.

question.erotisi: Which were the causes of the naval battle of Navarino?
question.sosti: the decision of the Great Powers for truce between the Greeks and the Ottoman empire
question.latos1: a naval episode between British and Turkish ships
question.latos2: the increase of the ships of the naval islands
question.sxolio: The Great Powers signed the Treaty of London in July of 1827, which was based on the appeal for Protection that the Greeks had made to England. The treaty provided also for the imposition of truce, if the opponents did not comply. The refusal of the Sublime Porte to accept the terms, paved the way to the naval battle of Navarino.

question.erotisi: Who were the Admirals representing the Great Powers in the naval battle of Navarino?
question.sosti: Edward Codrington, Login Heyden and Henry de Rigny
question.latos1: Edward Codrington, Abney Hastings and Henry de Rigny
question.latos2: Edward Codrington, Login Heyden and Charles Fabvier
question.sxolio: The English Edward Codrington, the Russian Login Heyden and the French Henry de Rigny were the three admirals who linked their name with the Naval Battle of Navarino. In commemoration of the event, three parallel streets in the center of Athens, near Victoria Square, bear their names.

question.erotisi: When did the naval battle of Navarino take place?
question.sxolio: Around the end of June the Great Powers sent naval squadrons in east Mediterranean, in order to impose their policy, but also to suppress piracy that affected the British commerce in east Mediterranean. The naval battle of Navarino took place on 8/20 October 1827.

question.erotisi: Which were the results of the naval battle of Navarino?
question.latos1: the crushing defeat of the Russo-English fleet
question.latos2: the suppression of the Greek Revolution
question.sxolio: The defeat of the Turkish-Egyptian fleet at Navarino and subsequently the defeat of the Ottoman empire in the Russo-Turkish war (1828-1829) forced the Sultan to accept the decisions of the Great Powers, which, motivated also by the desire to enhance their influence in the Balkans, decided to grant independence to the Greeks.

question.erotisi: Greece was recognized as independent state:
question.sxolio: Greece by the signing of the Protocol of London on 22 January/3 February 1830 is recognized as independent state with political, administrative and commercial rights.

question.erotisi: The borders of the Greek state were fixed in 1832:
question.sosti: along the Ambrakikos-Pagasitikos line. The Greek state included: the Peloponnese, Central (Sterea) Greece, the islands of the Argo-Saronic Gulf, Euboea, the Cyclades and the Sporades
question.latos1: at the estuaries of the Aspropotamos and Spercheios rivers. The Greek state included: the Peloponnese, Central (Sterea) Greece, Euboea and the Cyclades
question.latos2: at Elassona. The Greek state included the Peloponnese, Central (Sterea) Greece, Euboea and the Cyclades.
question.sxolio: After the signing of the Protocol of London, on 18/30 August 1832, the borders of the first Greek state were fixed along the Ambrakikos-Pagasitikos borderline.

question.erotisi: Ioannis Kapodistrias was elected governor of Greece:
question.sxolio: On 30 March 1827, in the Third National Assembly of Troezen, Ioannis Kapodistrias was elected governor of Greece for a seven-year term.

question.erotisi: Which body did Ioannis Kapodistrias found?
question.sxolio: «Panhellenion» was called the advisory body that was established on 18 January 1828 by Ioannis Kapodistrias, in the place of the Legislative, as one of the terms that he posed to undertake the position of authority. The Panhellenion was replaced by the Senate during the Fourth National Assembly of Argos, in July 1829.

question.erotisi: When and where did the last battle of the Revolution take place?
question.sxolio: When Ioannis Kapodistrias became Governor of Greece, the Revolution was still underway. For this reason he focused on the continuation of the military operations in Central (Sterea) Greece, in order to secure the expansion of the borders. On 12 September 1829 at Petra of Boeotia, the Greek forces under Dimitrios Ypsilantis defeated the Ottoman army.

question.erotisi: Ioannis Kapodistrias was assassinated:
question.sxolio: The administration of Kapodistrias provoked the reaction of the notables, the ship owners and the liberal intellectuals. He was assassinated on 27 September 1831 outside the church of Agios Spyridon in Nafplio by Konstantinos and Georgios Mavromichalis. His death was instant.

question.erotisi: Ludwig I was an admirer of the ancient Greek civilization and spirit. In an auction he had bought the sculptures that came from the temple:
question.sxolio: The sculptures are on display in the Munich Glyptothek, which was created by Ludwig I, to house his collection. Ludwig's great love for the ancient Greek art resulted in his adorning with Neo-Classical buildings Munich, which remained also known as "Athens of Isar" (Isar is the name the river that flows through Munich).

question.erotisi: After Otto became hereditary monarch of Greece, his father, king Ludwig of Bavaria, offered to Greece:
question.sxolio: Ludwig offered to the newly established Greek state an army of 3.500 Bavarians and allowed also the involvement of Bavarian officers in the organization of the army.

question.erotisi: Ludwig I was a member:
question.latos2: of the Society for the Promotion of Education and Learning
question.sxolio: As member of the Philomuse Society, Ludwig I participated actively in the preparation of the Revolution. In the years 1825-1826 took the initiative to send twelve officers of the Bavarian army as military advisors, unofficially, to Greece to help with the formation and training of the tactical Greek army.

question.erotisi: Who of the fighters were appointed members of the delegation that went to Munich, to offer the crown to the first king of Greece?
question.sosti: A. Miaoulis, K. Botsaris and D. Plapoutas
question.sxolio: In the similarly called representation of the Frieze in the Hall of the Trophies, Ludwig I is depicted introducing young Otto to the members of the Greek delegation.

question.erotisi: After the assassination of Ioannis Kapodistrias the Great Powers appointed as king of Greece Otto, the 17-year old son of the king of Bavaria, Ludwig I. When though did he take on his tasks?
question.sxolio: Because Otto was underage, the power was to be exercised until his coming of age (1835), by the Regency, a council of Bavarian officials, appointed by Otto's father.

question.erotisi: By the Treaty of London (25 April/ 7 May 1832) Otto was proclaimed:
question.sxolio: Otto was proclaimed king of Greece and not of the Greeks, so as not to raise issues in relation to those Greeks who were still unliberated.

question.erotisi: Otto arrived in Nafplio:
question.sxolio: It is said that, when Otto was about to step on the jetty, he stumbled, and this was deemed by the Greeks as a bad omen. His reception however was enthusiastic. Kolokotronis deposited symbolically his weapons at the feet of the young king.

question.erotisi: Otto died in 1867 and was buried:
question.sxolio: Otto was exiled in 1862 and departed for Munich, where he died in 1867. He was buried wearing, according to his wish, the Greek fustanella (a man's pleated skirt). After eight years Amalia died, too.
